intended_object: The standard fact that the evaluation functors `PresheafOfModules R ⥤ ModuleCat (R.obj X)` jointly reflect colimits. A cocone over a diagram of presheaves of modules is a colimit if, for each object X, its image under evaluation at X is a colimit. This is read off the docstring and the name, and matches the analogous `CategoryTheory.Limits.evaluationJointlyReflectsColimits` for functor categories.
explanation:
The definition takes a cocone `c` over `F : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules R`, together with, for every `X`, a proof that `(evaluation R X).mapCocone c` is a colimit. From these it builds `IsColimit c`:
- the descending map is defined objectwise from the colimits at each `X`;
- its naturality comes from the naturality of the cocone maps and the uniqueness of maps out of a colimit;
- the factorisation and uniqueness conditions are checked one component at a time.

This is exactly the mathematical statement in the docstring, at its natural generality: any category `C`, any presheaf of rings `R`, any index category `J`.

The `Limits.evaluationJointlyReflectsColimits` named as the counterpart is the same fact for functor categories. It does not directly apply here, because `PresheafOfModules R` is not literally a functor category (the module category changes with `X`). So the separate definition is justified.

One caveat. The section variable `PreservesColimit (F ⋙ evaluation R Y) (restrictScalars …)` could be pulled in automatically, since it only mentions variables the definition already uses, and the proof does not need it. However, the Batteries `unusedArguments` linter would flag an unused instance argument, and there is no nolint entry for this declaration. So it is probably not an actual argument. Even if it were, it holds in all the uses in the library, where it is found automatically. I am not confident enough to call this a real narrowing.

The construction is a proof-like piece of data, but it is the standard statement that evaluation jointly reflects colimits, and it is faithful to that statement.
